items.readme:
# dsh-superagent

> **Research prototype for reference only, not an official DeepSeek product.** This code grew out of our team's day-to-day development work, with much of the engineering done by coding agents. Treat it as research code, not production-ready software. It may still contain bugs, and its coding style and engineering practices may be inconsistent. Review and adapt it before using it in your own environment.
>
> We have adapted it for publication, so it is not identical to our internal version or the implementation described in *Exploring Super-agent Design: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System*. Some designs discussed in the article are directions for future development and are not implemented in this prototype.

dsh-superagent is a proactive coding agent for one GitHub repository, packaged as a bundle for [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/en/harness/). It listens to GitHub and, optionally, Feishu. When someone allowed asks the agent for work, it opens a work item, works on it in its own agent session and directory, and answers in the original conversation, for example with a pull request. A web panel shows what needs a person.

It is also a way of working with an agent: **take as little human attention as possible, and give as much value as possible.** An agent that can act for a whole team can also waste a whole team's attention, so it acts only when asked or when a rule the team wrote allows it, and speaks only when someone must act or can use a result. [docs/000-philosophy.md](docs/000-philosophy.md) explains the principle and what it asks of the operator.

## Setup

Setup has many steps, so an agent does it with you. Ask your coding agent:

> Read SETUP.md in this repository and set up dsh-superagent with me.

It asks one short question at a time, shows the full plan once, and then installs and configures everything. [SETUP.md](SETUP.md) is what it follows.

## Documentation

Read the numbered documents in order; each builds only on the ones before it.

- [000 Philosophy](docs/000-philosophy.md)
- [001 Domain model](docs/001-domain.md)
- [002 Authorization](docs/002-authorization.md)
- [003 Execution](docs/003-execution.md)
- [004 Prompts](docs/004-prompts.md)
- [005 Panel](docs/005-panel.md)
- [006 Deployment](docs/006-deployment.md): manual setup, configuration, upgrades and troubleshooting
- [007 Architecture](docs/007-architecture.md)
- [008 Cookbook](docs/008-cookbook.md): adding a Source

## Development

`pnpm check` runs the typecheck, the tests and the build.

items.readme:
Craft Anything

English · 日本語 · 简体中文 · 한국어

See how any website, app or game works, then have AI build your own version; an open-source, clean-room engine in pure Rust.
Point it at a target, say what you want, and it studies the original with real inspection tools,
has a coding agent build a new project, checks the result against the original and refines it.

Download Craft Anything · ArtCraft · All Crafting Apps



A website project: each check says how alike the build is, you approve anything outside the rules, and the plan shows what's left.

> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Painters, photographers, > filmmakers, illustrators, designers, animators, hobbyists, and people who picked up a pencil > last week. If you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

How it works · Two ways to use it · AI · Agents · Under the hood · Get started · Status · Downloads · Discord


🔍 Study anything

Websites, desktop apps, phone apps, games and files: real inspection tools find out how they're built and what they do, with the evidence behind every answer.

🛠️ Build your own

Say what you want ("Recreate this website", "Recreate this game's gameplay in Rust") and a coding agent builds a new project in the stack you ask for.

✅ Checked, not guessed

Every build is compared with the original (pages at three screen widths, a game's own self-test, an app's runs) and refined until it's close.

🤖 Agent-ready

314 tools, each one a CLI command and an MCP tool, so any agent can drive the same engine the app uses. No AI is needed to inspect.

## How it works Point Craft Anything at a target, say what you want, and press Start. It works in four steps, asking you in plain words when a decision is yours: 1. **Study:** inspect the original: its pages at every width, its code, its files, how it runs. 2. **Build:** a coding agent builds a new project, in the language, framework or engine your request names (or a sensible default). 3. **Check:** compare the build with the original and list what doesn't match yet. 4. **Ready:** open, play or preview the result, or ask for changes and it refines it.

Make: pick what to recreate, say what you want, press Start.
Ready: play the game, or ask for changes below.
## Two ways to use it - **Simple** (default): "What do you want to make?" Pick a website, app or game, describe it, press Start. A project page shows the four steps (Study → Build → Check → Ready), what the agent is doing in plain words, question and approval cards, how alike the result is, and buttons to open the result or its folder. Ask for changes in the box at the bottom. "Just look inside" opens a target for questions without building anything (in Deep mode). - **Advanced**: the full workbench: every tool (Ctrl/Cmd+K), functions, strings, pseudo-C, disassembly, hex, call graphs, evidence, unknowns, jobs, logs and the agent console. Both modes drive the same engine. ## Clean room or Deep - **Clean room** (the default): nothing inside the original is read, not its code, files or page source. Craft Anything works from what you can see: pictures you add, the website as a visitor sees it (screenshots, visible text, measured layout, colours, fonts and spacing, menus opened) and, when you allow it, a picture of the app's window. Tools that would look inside are refused and say how to turn on Deep mode. - **Deep**: every tool is used, for your private use. A program's code and files are read with the built-in engines (and Ghidra when it's installed), a website's JavaScript is read and its start page watched, and the builder may use all of them. Switch in the title bar or Settings, with `settings_set deep_mode true`, or for one CLI run with `--deep` (or `--clean-room`).


Advanced: functions, pseudo-C, the agent and the evidence behind every answer.

## AI Building needs a coding agent on your computer. **Claude Code** is supported first: Craft Anything runs your own, unmodified `claude` program, which uses your own sign-in; Craft Anything never sees or handles your account. Your use of it falls under your own agreement with Anthropic. See [docs/claude-code.md](docs/claude-code.md) for how and why. A Codex adapter exists but hasn't been verified on a real install yet. Other agents that speak ACP (Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, opencode, goose, Hermes, Maki) can be switched to it per backend; of those, only Maki has been run live. Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter and local OpenAI-compatible servers are available for questions and analysis (Settings → AI). ## Built for agents Every tool is also a CLI subcommand and an MCP tool, so an agent can study a target or run a whole rebuild without the app: ```sh craft-anything-cli commands # every tool, by toolset craft-anything-cli mcp # serve them to any MCP client craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website" ``` Results are evidence records with their confidence, coverage and limitations; big ones come back as a summary first and are paged with `core_evidence_browse`. `craft-anything-cli setup` connects Craft Anything to coding-agent apps. ## Under the hood A pure-Rust reverse-engineering engine with 314 tools (298 in the engine, the rest from the AI and setup layers) for native programs, .NET, Java, Android, Apple, Electron/JavaScript, websites, firmware, packet captures, databases and game files. Its own decoders, disassembler and decompiler work without any outside program; Deep mode uses them all, and Ghidra when it's installed. It powers the desktop app (egui), the CLI and the MCP server, and parts of it run in the browser as WebAssembly. The full list is in [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md). ## Get started Requires Rust **1.97 or newer** (a dependency needs it; `rustup update`). On Debian or Ubuntu, the desktop app also needs: ```sh sudo apt-get install libxkbcommon-dev libwayland-dev libx11-dev libxrandr-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev libgtk-3-dev ``` Then: ```sh git clone https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything && cd craft-anything cargo run --release -p craft-anything # the desktop app cargo install --path apps/craft-anything-cli # the CLI, as `craft-anything-cli` craft-anything-cli doctor # checks the install, coding agents and engines ``` Building needs a coding agent signed in on your computer (see [AI](#ai)); `doctor` says what's missing. Rebuild from the command line (questions are asked in the terminal): ```sh craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Recreate this website" craft-anything-cli rebuild - "A snake game in Rust" --rounds 1 craft-anything-cli rebuild https://example.com "Make the header blue" --continue-in "" craft-anything-cli rebuild - "Add a contact form" --project-folder "" --existing edit ``` New projects go in `Documents/Craft Anything` (change it in Settings → General). Each project folder holds `craft.json` (the request, target, status and history), `capture/` (what was recorded from the target), `app/` (the generated project), `checks/` (each comparison against the original), `investigation.cany/` (evidence) and `inbox/` (open questions). A project can also start in a folder you pick (Choose a folder… under Start, or `--project-folder`). If it already has files, you say what they are: the app itself, which the builder edits in place, or material to start from, with the app built in `app/` beside them (Settings → General can remember the answer). Settings → General also lists projects from more folders; removing one only takes it off the list. ## Status > [!IMPORTANT] > **Status:** Craft Anything is in early alpha. What works today, what is partial and what's next: > > - **Works today:** the desktop app (Simple and Advanced), the CLI and the MCP server; the > Study → Build → Check → Refine workflow for websites, apps and games with Claude Code as the > builder; website checks at three screen widths; game rebuilds in Unity, Unreal or Godot; Deep > mode with Ghidra; generated pictures and 3D models (opt-in, your own fal.ai key); plugins (MCP > servers, and WASM components in builds with the `wasm-plugins` option). > - **Partly there:** building with API keys and other coding agents (built, not yet run live), > behaviour checks for apps and games, a few engine tools tested only against stand-ins. > - **Next:** the first public release (installers for Windows, macOS, Linux and FreeBSD, and the > browser viewer are set up in CI), then the managed tier. > > [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) has the detail and how each part was checked, > [docs/tool-status.md](docs/tool-status.md) the tool-by-tool checklist, and > [docs/ROADMAP.md](docs/ROADMAP.md) the plan, item by item. Please file issues, or tell us what > broke on [Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft). **Responsible use.** Use Craft Anything on software you own or are allowed to examine. It never bypasses DRM, logins or anti-cheat. Rebuilds recreate layout, style and behaviour from evidence; the agent is told not to copy logos, photos or text unless you confirm you own them or have permission. ## Downloads On GitHub, the [latest release](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/latest) has every build listed below, and [all releases](https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases) has earlier versions and their notes. `` in the file names is the version number, and `SHA256SUMS.txt` lists a checksum for every file. ### Windows | Build | Installer | Portable | |---|---|---| | x64 (64-bit Intel/AMD) | `craft-anything--windows-x64.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-x64-portable.zip` | | arm64 (Snapdragon and other ARM PCs) | `craft-anything--windows-arm64.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-arm64-portable.zip` | | x86 (32-bit) | `craft-anything--windows-x86.msi` | `craft-anything--windows-x86-portable.zip` | Installers and executables are code-signed. The portable zip keeps its settings next to the app. ### macOS | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | App, universal (Apple silicon + Intel) | `craft-anything--macos-universal.dmg` | Signed and notarized | | Command-line tool, universal | `craft-anything-cli--macos-universal.zip` | Signed and notarized; see below if macOS blocks it | Versions after 0.2.0 include the command-line tool in the app, so builds don't need the separate zip. You only need it to use the command line without the app. A browser download of the zip can stop with "Apple could not verify craft-anything-cli" (a lone program can't carry its notarization with it, so macOS has to look it up online). A download from the terminal isn't checked this way, so use this instead: ```sh ver=0.2.0 # change this to the version you want curl -fLO "https://github.com/storytold/craft-anything/releases/download/v$ver/craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal.zip" ditto -x -k "craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal.zip" . mkdir -p ~/.local/bin mv "craft-anything-cli-$ver-macos-universal/craft-anything-cli" ~/.local/bin/ ~/.local/bin/craft-anything-cli --version ``` To run it as just `craft-anything-cli`, add `~/.local/bin` to your `PATH`. If you already have the blocked copy, press Done (not Move to Bin), then run `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine `, or allow it in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. ### Linux | Format | x86_64 | aarch64 (ARM64) | Notes | |---|---|---|---| | AppImage | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.AppImage` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.AppImage` | Runs anywhere; updates itself with [AppImageUpdate](https://github.com/AppImageCommunity/AppImageUpdate) (`.zsync` files) | | Flatpak | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.flatpak` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.flatpak` | Sandboxed; `flatpak install --user ` | | Debian/Ubuntu | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.deb` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.deb` | | | Fedora/RHEL/openSUSE | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.rpm` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.rpm` | | | Tarball | `craft-anything--linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | `craft-anything--linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | Unpack anywhere | RISC-V (riscv64): `craft-anything--linux-riscv64.tar.gz`, a tarball only. ### FreeBSD | Build | File | |---|---| | x86_64 | `craft-anything--freebsd-x86_64.tar.gz` | ### Web (WebAssembly) | Build | File | Notes | |---|---|---| | Browser viewer | `craft-anything-web-.zip` | Says what a file is, in the browser (the file never leaves it); host the folder on any static web server ([packaging/web/README.md](packaging/web/README.md)) |

items.readme: # pixelfx. **232 pixel art effects and animations, every one a small piece of code.** Fire, explosions, magic, weather, UI, pickups, critters and more. Play them live, recolor and mirror them, drop them into a browser game, or export sprite sheets for any engine. Plus a Claude Code skill that makes new ones the way a picky pixel artist would: draft, render, look, refine. **[open the gallery](https://patch-gg.github.io/pixelfx/)** · [catalog](docs/CATALOG.md) · [the skill](#the-skill) · [make your own](#make-your-own) · [how it works](#how-it-works) The method is [Hugo Duprez](https://x.com/HugoDuprez)'s, from [How to make (good) pixel art effects with Claude](https://www.spritefusion.com/blog/how-to-make-good-pixel-art-effects-with-claude): code is clay, trust your eyes, feed your references. His [open-source effects](https://www.spritefusion.com/pixel-art-vfx) at Sprite Fusion set the bar, and `src/core/sim.js` and the effects that say so at the top adapt his code. This repo is our take on the idea at library scale, with a skill to keep going. ## what's in it. | category | effects | some of them | |---|---|---| | **fire** | 12 | brazier, campfire, candle, fire breath, fire ring, fire tornado… | | **explosions** | 12 | barrel explosion, big explosion, cartoon pow, dirt explosion, firework burst, firework rocket… | | **water** | 12 | bubbles, drip, fountain, geyser, rain splash, ripples… | | **ice** | 10 | blizzard vortex, freeze, frost breath, frost nova, ice crystal, ice lance… | | **lightning** | 11 | ball lightning, chain lightning, charge up, electrified, lightning strike, plasma ball… | | **sci-fi** | 12 | emp blast, energy core, force field, glitch, hologram, jetpack… | | **melee** | 12 | claw swipe, dagger flurry, double slash, hammer smash, heavy cleave, scythe reap… | | **impacts** | 11 | blunt hit, bullet impact, critical hit, ground slam, heavy landing, hit flash… | | **projectiles** | 13 | arrow, bullet tracer, cannon shot, energy disc, signal flare, homing missile… | | **spawn & death** | 10 | coin drop, disintegrate, dissolve burn, egg hatch, poof, respawn beam… | | **arcane** | 12 | arcane beam, arcane missiles, arcane orb, blink in, blink out, magic circle cast… | | **holy** | 10 | blessing, divine shield, feather burst, halo, heal, healing ring… | | **shadow** | 12 | black hole, curse, dark explosion, eclipse, grasping hands, hex sigil… | | **status** | 13 | bleeding, burning, charmed, confused, cursed, frozen… | | **nature** | 13 | acid splash, boulder, earth spike, healing bloom, leaf storm, poison cloud… | | **weather** | 12 | aurora, blizzard, cherry blossoms, clouds, falling leaves, fireflies… | | **ui** | 12 | achievement, coin collect, combo counter, confetti, countdown, crit number… | | **pickups** | 11 | chest open, coin spin, collect burst, crystal shard, gem spin, heart pickup… | | **transitions** | 10 | blinds, burn away, crt off, diamond wipe, glitch wipe, iris… | | **critters** | 12 | bat, bird, butterfly, eyeball, fish school, flying skull… | Every effect is a file in `src/fx//.js`. The [catalog](docs/CATALOG.md) lists them all. ## use one. **In a browser game** (canvas, Phaser, PixiJS, Kaplay, three.js), use the code. No dependencies. ```js import { createFrame, clearFrame, createFx, composite } from "pixelfx"; import * as frostNova from "pixelfx/fx/ice/frost-nova"; const frame = createFrame(320, 180); // your game's pixel resolution const img = new ImageData(320, 180); const fx = createFx(frostNova, { x: 160, y: 140 }); // also: flip, angle, seed, palette, light... function tick(dt) { fx.update(dt); clearFrame(frame); fx.draw(frame, "back"); // behind characters drawCharacters(); fx.draw(frame, "front"); composite(frame, img.data, backgroundColor); // color, then light added on top ctx.putImageData(img, 0, 0); // scale up with image-rendering: pixelated } ``` Install from GitHub with `npm i github:patch-gg/pixelfx`, or copy `src/core` and the effects you want. **In any engine** (Godot, Unity, GameMaker, Defold, LÖVE, Bevy), use sprite sheets: ```bash node tools/render.mjs ice/frost-nova --sheet ``` That writes a transparent PNG of every frame in a grid and an Aseprite-style JSON (frame rects, durations, and `meta.pixelfx` with fps, loop, columns and the pivot). Phaser's atlas loader and the Aseprite importers for Godot and Unity read it. `node tools/sheets.mjs` exports the whole library to `sheets/`. Any effect takes a `palette` (a dark-to-bright ramp of hex colors), so a fire can burn blue and a heal can glow pink without touching its code: ```bash node tools/render.mjs fire/torch --gif --opts '{"palette": ["#102","#215","#43a","#8cf","#cff","#fff"]}' ``` ## the skill. The `pixelfx` skill teaches Claude Code to find, use, export and make effects. Install it as a plugin: ``` /plugin marketplace add patch-gg/pixelfx /plugin install pixelfx@pixelfx ``` or copy `skills/pixelfx` into `~/.claude/skills/`. Then ask for what you want: - "Add a frost nova to my mage's ultimate." - "Make five takes on a coin pickup sparkle and show me the best two." - "Export the fire and explosions categories as sprite sheets for Godot." - "This hit effect feels floaty. Make it punchier." ## make your own. ```bash node tools/new.mjs arcane/my-spell # a working starting point (add --loop for a loop) node tools/render.mjs arcane/my-spell # records/arcane/my-spell/contact.png: look at it node tools/check.mjs arcane/my-spell # spills, seams, unseeded randomness, slow frames ``` Then go round: look at the contact sheet, fix the worst thing, render again. `--gif` and `--mp4` show the motion, `--all` shows every frame. [docs/AUTHORING.md](docs/AUTHORING.md) has the contract, the drawing API and the quality bar. `node tools/serve.mjs` runs the gallery locally with your effects in it. ## how it works. - **Two kinds of effect, no images.** Pure effects export `draw(p, t, o)`, the frame at `t` seconds from `t` alone, so loops tile with no seam. Simulated effects export `create(o)` and step real particles, debris and lights at 120 Hz, so sparks bounce and smoke rolls the same at any frame rate. - **Two buffers.** `color` takes pixels: opaque, dithered or truly translucent. `light` takes additive glow, added on top. Hot things look hot because of the light buffer. - **Seeded everything.** Every random number comes from the effect's seed, so frame 40 is the same every time. - **Local space.** Effects draw around their own origin; the painter places, mirrors and rotates them. Directional effects face right. A 24×38 stock character stands in for status effects, auras and hits. - **Same frame shape as Sprite Fusion's VFX** (`{ w, h, ox, oy, color, light }`), so both libraries can draw into one frame. ## license. MIT, code and effects. Use them in anything, commercial included. Parts are adapted from Hugo Duprez's MIT effects, and the Patch Pixel font in `gallery/fonts` is Patch's own and not covered: see [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). Made by [Patch](https://patch.gg).

# Agent Autoloop **让你的命令行 Agent 在后台自己接活、自己跟进到底；平时不烦你，遇到拿不准的事才发卡片找你拍板。** **中文** | [English](README.en.md) [上手](#上手) · [场景模板](#拿来即用的场景模板) · [插件](#插件体系四个方向都能自由替换) · [内核](#内核的四个机制) · [文档](#更多文档) ![架构图](docs/architecture.svg) ## 它解决什么问题？ 平时我们用 Claude Code、Codex 这类命令行 Agent，大多是“人守着终端用”：你输一句话，盯着它跑，等它问你下一步；一旦关掉窗口或者人走开，事情就断了。 **Agent Autoloop** 是一个极轻量的自动化中台。它把任务调度做成一个零外部依赖的**内核**，把事件来源、Agent、通知通道，甚至代码上线流水线全部拆成可随时插拔的**插件**。 - **一台电脑、一条命令就能跑。** 装在你的 Mac 或 Linux 上，不用买云服务器，也不用开放公网端口。 - **一行配置接新 Agent。** 不需要 SDK，也不需要改 Agent 源码，能接收提示词并打印最后一条回复的命令行工具都能接。 - **没有后台界面。** 需要你拍板时把卡片推到飞书、钉钉、企微、Slack、Discord 或桌面通知；想看全局进展，敲一行命令。 ## 上手 支持 macOS 和 Linux。运行前需要装好 Node 24、Git、curl，以及任意一个你已经登录好的命令行 Agent，不需要 GitHub 账号。也可以直接把[安装说明](INSTALL.md)丢给你的 Agent，让它替你装好。 > **Windows 版：待定。** 很多朋友在问 Windows 版，我都看到了。我现在人在外面出差，手边没有 Windows 电脑，没法真机开发和测试，所以现在还不能在 Windows 上用。这个周末（11 月 7、8 日）回家后，我会把它开发完，做完兼容性测试，再正式推出。进度会更新在 [#17](https://github.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop/issues/17)。 ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop/main/install.sh | sh ``` 装好后用你本机的 Agent 真实走一遍“提问 → 退出等回复 → 拍板 → 接着干完”： ```bash agent-autoloop try ``` 下面是在终端里的真实输出： ```text 事件发出去了，Agent 开始干活…… Agent 结束了这一轮，问了你一个问题。它现在不占进程、不花 Token。 【等你决定】#1 试跑：选一个颜色 这是一次试跑，选哪个都行。 1. 蓝色 2. 绿色 回答：agent-autoloop answer 1 <序号> 答完运行 agent-autoloop status，能看到它接着把活干完。 ``` 交互终端里直接输入数字回车；非交互终端运行 `agent-autoloop answer 1 2` 选择“绿色”。再跑 `agent-autoloop status`，就能看到它接上刚才的会话并显示“你选了绿色，试跑通过”，还有今天和最近 7 天的轮数、Token 和费用（[统计口径](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#看情况回答)）。 ## 一件事怎么转起来 编号和上面的架构图一一对应： 1. **新事件进来。** 早上 9 点的定时任务、GitHub 上新提的 Issue、业务系统报的错，都变成一条标准事件送进内核。 2. **按规则派活。** 内核照你写的规则，决定交给哪个 Agent、去哪个目录干。同一件事排队时又来的消息，会合并成一轮处理。 3. **干完一轮就退出。** Agent 把结果写在最后一条回复里，进程直接退出。 4. **拿不准才问你。** 碰到删数据、重启服务、花钱、对外发消息这类事，内核通过飞书或桌面通知发一张卡片给你。等你回复期间，它不占后台进程，也不消耗 Token。 5. **点一下，接着干。** 你选完，它接上原来的对话，把剩下的活干完。 能自己搞定的事走图上方的自动闭环：直接办完，或者约个时间（比如半小时后）再醒来复查，全程不打扰你。 ## 日常怎么配？ ### 写一份规则（`rules.json`） 不需要写胶水代码。打开 `~/.agent-autoloop/rules.json`，在 `rules` 里写清楚**什么事、交给谁、在哪个目录干**。`to` 填 `agents` 里已有的名字。比如每天早上 9 点写早报： ```json { "name": "早报", "when": { "cron": "0 9 * * *" }, "to": "codex", "cwd": "~/notes", "prompt": "整理昨天的笔记和提交，写今天的早报。" } ``` 外部事件写法一样，只是要先接好来源。比如有人提新 Issue 时交给 Codex，先按[说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个事件插件)在 `sources` 里登记 `github`： ```json { "name": "处理 issue", "when": { "source": "github", "types": ["issues.opened"] }, "to": "codex", "cwd": "~/code/app", "skill": "handle-issue", "parallel": 3 } ``` 保存后几秒内自动生效，可以运行 `agent-autoloop check` 检查。就算改错了，或者文件被删、读不到，系统也会继续按旧规则跑，并发卡片提醒你。 ### Agent 怎么跟中台配合？ 中台对 Agent 只有一个约定：**在最后一条回复里交代结果**。事情办完了，正常输出一句结论就行。需要向你请示时，在回复末尾附一段 `agent-autoloop` 代码块： ````text 订单已经核对完毕，库存充足。 ```agent-autoloop { "ask": [{ "title": "怎么发货？", "text": "两种方式今天都能发出。", "options": ["快递", "自提"], "key": "shipping" }] } ``` ```` 除了提问（`ask`），还能发通知（`notice`）、关闭已解决的卡片（`resolve`）、预约复查（`later`）和触发新事件（`events`）。通告不需要回答，但结案时可以顺手写一句处理说明，这句话会留在卡片上。万一 JSON 写错了，中台只让它在原会话里重写最后这段回复，不会把已经干完的业务重做一遍；重写也失败时，保留原结论并通知你回执没有生效。接着旧会话跑也一样：会话接不上才开新的；接上了、干到一半断了，就算没跑成，过几分钟回到原会话重试，不开新会话重做。 ## 拿来即用的场景模板 每套模板都带规则、任务 Skill 和启用说明。 | 想做什么 | 已经封装好的流程 | |---|---| | [每日早报](examples/recipes/morning-brief/README.md) | 默认每天 8 点整理本地笔记和 Git 提交，写入 `briefs/YYYY-MM-DD.md` | | [跟进 GitHub Issue](examples/recipes/github-issues/README.md) | 每 5 分钟查新 Issue，在本地改代码并通知你查看；不提交、不推送、不回复 Issue | | [线上告警排查](examples/recipes/ops-alerts/README.md) | 接收报错、对照代码查原因，需要重启时发卡片询问，回答后继续 | | [用户反馈处理](examples/recipes/feedback/README.md) | 重读反馈当前状态、修复、交付核实、准备回复；需要决定时飞书问你，回答后继续 | | [网站巡检](examples/recipes/website-watch/README.md) | 每 5 分钟检查状态和关键内容，首次异常交给 Agent，持续异常不重复通知，恢复后更新原卡片 | | [飞书周报与业务摘要](examples/recipes/feishu-brief/README.md) | 周日 18 点按你的权限读汇报和指定表格，生成本地摘要；飞书只发简短摘要，完整稿留在本机 | | [PR 自动交付](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#交付流水线) | 打上 `deliver` 标签后，审查、等 CI、合并、等发布并核对线上版本 | **启用：** 打开对应说明，把任务 Skill 放进所用 Agent 的 skills 目录，把示例规则合入 `~/.agent-autoloop/rules.json`，替换电脑名和路径，再运行 `agent-autoloop check`。 反馈处理、网站巡检和飞书摘要默认使用北京时间，只发给本人的飞书私聊。样例数据都是虚构的；脚本和回执只用本地 HTTP 与假飞书 CLI 验证过，没有在真实账号上跑过完整业务。 更多模板：[Claude 委托 Codex 处理网页](examples/recipes/browser-handoff/README.md)、[每周代码清理](examples/skills/weekly-sweep/SKILL.md)、[交付 PR](examples/skills/ship-pr/SKILL.md)。 ## 插件体系：四个方向都能自由替换 内置插件随程序安装，填好配置即可启用；第三方插件用 `agent-autoloop add ` 安装。 | 方向 | 内置 | 配置 | |---|---|---| | **事件**：怎么发现新活 | [GitHub Webhook](plugins/github/source.ts)、[GitLab Webhook](plugins/gitlab/source.ts)、[HTTP 接口](docs/protocol.md#来源把世界变成事件)、[定时规则](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#改规则)、[Issue 轮询脚本](examples/watch-github-issues.sh) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个事件插件) | | **Agent**：谁来干活 | [Claude Code](plugins/claude/agent.ts)、[Codex](plugins/codex/agent.ts)、[ACP](plugins/acp/agent.ts)、[通用命令](plugins/command/agent.ts) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个-agent) | | **通道**：去哪找你拍板 | [桌面通知](plugins/desktop/channel.ts)（默认开启）、[飞书](plugins/feishu/channel.ts)、[钉钉 / 企微 / Slack / Discord](plugins/webhook/templates.ts) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#接一个通道) | | **交付**：把 CI/CD 也做成插件 | [`delivery`](plugins/delivery/delivery.ts) | [说明](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#交付流水线) | **实测情况：** Claude Code、Codex 和 ACP（官方 Codex ACP 适配器）跑通了多轮问答和跨进程会话续接；飞书跑通了发送、按钮回调和卡片更新；四种 Webhook 模板只在本地模拟服务上验证过，GitLab Webhook 按官方文档的格式测试，没连过真实 GitLab。这些文字通道靠回答链接拍板，要把 `hub.publicUrl` 配成手机或电脑能打开的地址。 **其他命令行 Agent 一行接入。** 设置 `use: "command"` 并传入命令数组，`{prompt}` 作为独立参数传递，不会被当成 shell 代码执行。下面的命令整理自各家官方文档，我们还没有逐个跑过： | Agent | 接入命令 | |---|---| | [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/docs/cli-help.md#dsh-headless) | `dsh --profile headless {prompt}` | | [pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/blob/main/packages/coding-agent/docs/cli.md) | `pi --print {prompt}` | | [OpenClaw](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/agent) | `openclaw agent exec {prompt}` | | [Hermes](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/cli) | `hermes chat -q {prompt}` | | [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/cli/reference/parameters) | `agent -p --trust {prompt}` | | [WorkBuddy / CodeBuddy](https://www.codebuddy.ai/docs/cli/headless) | `codebuddy -p {prompt}` | **交付流水线。** 给 GitHub PR 打上 `deliver` 标签后，它会自己跟进到上线：**审代码 → 等 CI → 合并 PR → 等部署 → 核对线上版本**。审查和交付配置只从 `main` 读取，绝不在接单电脑上检出或运行 PR 里的代码；排队、并发和重试直接复用内核。 **写自己的插件。** 从 [Agent](examples/plugins/hello-agent/agent.ts)、[通道](examples/plugins/hello-channel/channel.ts)、[事件](examples/plugins/hello-source/source.ts) 三个可运行的最小模板开始，见[插件开发说明](docs/plugins.md)。要让 Agent 操作网页，先看[浏览器接入](docs/plugins.md#浏览器接入)。命令行和 [MCP](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md#mcp-与密钥撤销) 也能查看和回答卡片。 ## 内核的四个机制 内核约 1650 行代码、零运行时依赖。它不读系统时钟、不用随机数、不向外发请求，插件主动连进来，账号凭据留在各自的插件里；同样的输入永远得出同样的结果。它把四个计算机领域的成熟做法用到了命令行 Agent 上： - **挂起零消耗**：等你拍板时进程直接退出，等待状态存在数据库里，Agent 不用一直挂着。你三天没回，这三天就没有 Agent 进程在跑、不花 Token，只有很轻的中台在后台等着；你一回答，它接着原来的对话继续干。 - **事件溯源**：所有状态都从一条只追加的日志算出来，日志和索引在同一个事务里写进磁盘，写完才应答。进程被强杀，已经确认的事不丢（整机断电没有单独测过）；任何一轮为什么跑、结果是什么，一条命令就能查清；数据格式变了就从日志重建，不用写迁移脚本。 - **指令数据分离**：思路和 SQL 参数化一样。Issue 的标题和正文等外部文字只作为资料放进文件，不拼进提示词，提示词里只有校验过字符的类型、编号和链接；用哪个 Agent、在哪个目录、什么权限，只由你本机的规则决定，事件里带 `cwd`、`agent`、`access` 字段会被直接拒收。 - **跳数熔断**：思路和网络包的 TTL 一样。Agent 交回的事件会再派给 Agent，层数一路累加，经过人工提问和定时复查也不清零，Agent 自己改不了；超过 8 层就只记录、不再派活，并发一张卡片告诉你。 ### 自己跑一遍 在程序目录 `~/.agent-autoloop/app` 下运行： | 验证什么 | 命令 | |---|---| | 任何一轮的来龙去脉 | `agent-autoloop why 1` | | 20 万步模拟断网、丢包、崩溃和重复提交，一个种子就能复现 | `node sim/random.ts 24301 200000` | | 强杀进程 1000 次，已确认的记录一条不丢 | `node sim/crash.ts 1000 12648430` | | 下面的性能数字 | `npm run benchmark` | ```text 第 1 轮 · 演示 11-03 20:47:25 规则版本 #1 11-03 20:47:25 触发事件：来源 local · 类型 demo.start · 对象 example 11-03 20:47:25 local 领取（演示程序） 11-03 20:47:25 结束：演示完成 ``` ### 实测性能 Apple M5 Pro、24 GB、Node 24.21.0。写入逐条提交，事务落盘后才应答。`npm run benchmark` 的达标线按这台机器定，换台机器可能报未达标。 | 指标 | 实测 | |---|---:| | 冷启动 | 88.78 ms | | 空闲内存 | 59.94 MB RSS | | 1000 个同时等待的长轮询 | 170.49 MB RSS | | 持久化写入 | 2394 条/秒 | | 派活 p99 | 1.82 ms | | 排队 5000 时被挡下的心跳 p99 | 1.66 ms | | 110 万条事实时的启动 | 99.8 ms | | 内核行数（含空行和注释） | 1651 | | 运行时依赖 | 0 | 历史变大后，状态汇总会变慢，日志和索引也继续占磁盘；格式变化后的首次启动要从日志全量重建，110 万条用时 43.1 秒。[完整数据和测法](docs/protocol.md#历史增长实测)。 ## 用量与合规说明 中台直接调用你本机已经安装并登录好的命令行工具，不会读取或转存你的账号凭据。模型调用消耗算在你自己的账号名下，额度和使用范围遵循各家模型厂商的服务条款。 在高频自动化场景下，各家厂商通常更建议使用 API Key（个人订阅额度主要是为日常人工交互设计的，详见 [Anthropic](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/legal-and-compliance) 与 [OpenAI](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth) 的官方说明）。如果你用它对外提供服务，请使用 API Key。本项目为独立开源项目，与上述厂商无隶属或背书关系。 ## 更多文档 - [安装说明](INSTALL.md) - [规则与交付流水线配置手册](skills/agent-autoloop/SKILL.md) - [如何编写插件](docs/plugins.md) - [完整通信协议](docs/protocol.md) - [安全边界说明](SECURITY.md) - # NOIR

[![build](https://github.com/Verlintas/NOIR/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Verlintas/NOIR/actions/workflows/build.yml)
[![release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Verlintas/NOIR)](https://github.com/Verlintas/NOIR/releases)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/github/license/Verlintas/NOIR)](LICENSE)
![platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/platforms-macOS%20%7C%20Windows%20%7C%20Linux-2ea44f)
[![AtomGit](https://img.shields.io/badge/AtomGit-Verlintas%2FNOIR-2f81f7)](https://atomgit.com/Verlintas/NOIR)

**把「这台手机到底能泄露什么」变成一份可复现的报告。**

NOIR 是一个跑在电脑上的审计工具，通过 `adb` 读取已连接 Android 设备的应用清单、权限和 APK 里的网络端点，给出分类、风险评分和可执行的处置建议。它也可以在需要时调用 `jadx` 对单个应用做反编译和关键字检索。

> 定位：**审计与自我防护**。面向自己的设备、自己的应用、已授权的安全研究。

**官网 / Website:** https://verlintas.dev/noir/ · [中文](https://verlintas.dev/noir/zh/)

**AtomGit 镜像 / Mirror:** https://atomgit.com/Verlintas/NOIR

---

## 它做什么

1. **盘点**：列出所有「有网络权限 + 敏感权限」的应用，以及它们各自拿到了什么。
2. **抽取端点**：在设备端用 `unzip + strings` 从每个 APK 的 dex 里提取 URL，只回传几 KB，不把整包拉回电脑。
3. **分类与打分**：按包名和域名识别厂商（Xiaomi / Google / 腾讯 / 高德 …）与类别（遥测、广告、定位、输入法 …），结合权限和上报端点计算风险分。
4. **数据关联**：把权限翻译成"能拿到什么数据"（位置/通讯录/短信/通话/麦克风/相机/屏幕/应用列表/设备标识/文件/日历/账号），再和上报域名配对，得出"哪类数据可能流向哪里"。
5. **共享 UID**：识别 `android.uid.system` 这类共享用户，列出哪些包实际上共享同一套权限并集。
6. **清单层**：解析 `AndroidManifest.xml` 二进制 AXML，找出没有权限保护的导出组件、明文流量、备份、debuggable、targetSdk。
4. **给建议**：区分「可安全自动执行」「需人工确认」「不建议动」，并为每条动作生成回滚命令。
5. **必要时深挖**：`deep` 会把单个 APK 拉到本地，用 `jadx` 反编译后检索 `Runtime.exec`、`setApplicationEnabledSetting`、`DexClassLoader`、`MediaProjection` 等高风险调用。

## 它不做什么

- 不联网、不上传任何数据、不需要账号。
- 不修改系统分区，不需要 root。
- 不会自动卸载任何东西，除非你显式加 `--aggressive`。

---

## 第一次运行

```bash
noir
```

不带参数会进入向导：

1. 检查 `adb`，没有就**问你要不要自动下载**（`~/.noir/tools`）
2. 检查设备，没有就打印**开发者模式 / USB 调试的开通步骤**，然后**等你插线**（最多 180 秒）
3. 问一句「开始扫描?」，扫完直接出仪表盘
4. 问一句「执行这 19 条安全处置?」，`y` 就执行，并写好回滚文件

全程只会问两三个 y/n，其余都是自动的。

## 环境自检

```bash
noir doctor
```

```
NOIR doctor
  platform  Mac OS X aarch64
  java      17.0.19
  adb       /opt/homebrew/.../platform-tools/adb
            Version 37.0.1-15733141
  device    178b0d2f  device  2509FPN0BC
  jadx      /opt/homebrew/bin/jadx
```

```bash
noir setup          # 缺什么下什么
noir setup --yes    # 不询问，适合脚本
```

## 出现问题时

所有错误都会带「怎么办」，而不是抛异常栈：

```
╭─ ERROR ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ 指定的 adb 不存在：/nonexistent/adb                              │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ 检查路径，或运行 noir setup 自动安装。                           │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

没有设备时给出的是可执行步骤：

```
╭─ 没有检测到设备 ──────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  1. 打开开发者模式                                           │
│     小米 / HyperOS：设置 → 我的设备 → 全部参数 → 连点「MIUI 版本」7 次
│  2. 开启 USB 调试：设置 → 系统 → 开发者选项 → USB 调试        │
│  3. 插线后手机弹「允许 USB 调试吗？」→ 勾选「一律允许」        │
│  4. 还不行就换一根数据线（很多线只能充电）                    │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
```

已连接但没授权时，会单独提示「撤销 USB 调试授权后重插」。

## 支持平台

| 系统 | 状态 |
|---|---|
| macOS (Intel / Apple Silicon) | ✅ |
| Windows 10 / 11 | ✅ |
| Debian / Ubuntu | ✅ |

依赖：

- **JDK 17+**
- **Android platform-tools**（`adb`）
- **jadx**（仅 `deep` 命令需要）

程序会自动在常见安装位置查找 `adb` 和 `jadx`；找不到时可以用 `--adb` / `--jadx` 指定。

```bash
# macOS
brew install --cask android-platform-tools jadx

# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo apt install adb
# jadx: https://github.com/skylot/jadx/releases

# Windows (scoop)
scoop install adb jadx
```

---

## 安装

**方式一：下载即用（推荐）**

到 [Releases](https://github.com/Verlintas/NOIR/releases) 下载对应平台的 portable 包：

```
noir-v0.1.1-macOS-portable.zip
noir-v0.1.1-Windows-portable.zip
noir-v0.1.1-Linux-portable.zip
SHA256SUMS.txt
```

解压后**双击启动器**即可，包内自带运行时，**不需要安装 Java**：

| 系统 | 双击这个 | 如果被拦 |
|---|---|---|
| macOS | `Start NOIR.command` | 右键 → 打开；或 `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "Start NOIR.command" NOIR.app` |
| Windows | `Start NOIR.bat` | SmartScreen → 更多信息 → 仍要运行（批处理会切到 UTF-8 并调用包内 JRE） |
| Linux | `Start-NOIR.sh` | 先 `chmod +x Start-NOIR.sh`，或在终端执行 |

启动器会打开一个终端窗口跑完向导，并在结束时停住（不会一闪而过）。

`adb` 和 `jadx` 不在包里——首次运行会询问是否自动下载到 `~/.noir/tools`。

**方式二：从源码构建**

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Verlintas/NOIR
cd NOIR
./gradlew :cli:installDist
./cli/build/install/noir/bin/noir --about
```

## 构建

```bash
git clone <repo> && cd NOIR
./gradlew :cli:installDist
```

产物：

```
cli/build/install/noir/bin/noir        # macOS / Linux
cli/build/install/noir/bin/noir.bat    # Windows
```

也可以直接：

```bash
./gradlew :cli:run --args="devices"
```

---

## 界面

![NOIR dashboard on a Xiaomi 17 Pro Max](docs/screenshot.png)

真机输出（macOS Terminal）：渐变 logo、CJK 对齐的表格、按风险着色的分数、
每处理完一个 APK 就刷新一次的进度条。

`noir ui` 会把结果渲染成一块等宽仪表盘；颜色和边框都会按终端能力自动降级：

- `--ascii`：纯 ASCII 边框，给旧版 Windows 控制台
- `--no-color` / `--color`：关闭或强制 ANSI 颜色（默认按是否为 TTY 自动判断）
- `--quiet`：只留仪表盘，不打印扫描过程
- `--no-clear`：不清屏（方便把输出重定向到文件）

## 用法

```bash
noir --about              # 它是什么、会写什么、许可
noir --version
noir devices
noir scan                 # 全量扫描，输出 JSON / Markdown / 域名清单
noir ui                   # 扫描并渲染仪表盘
noir auto                 # 扫描 + 分类 + 生成处置计划（dry-run）
noir auto --apply         # 执行安全的 appops 动作（可回滚）
noir auto --apply --aggressive   # 额外卸载被标记的用户应用
noir deep com.example.app # 拉包 + jadx + 关键字检索
noir block com.example.app        # 打印处置命令
noir block com.example.app --apply
```

常用参数：

| 参数 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `--serial <id>` | 指定设备 |
| `--out <dir>` | 输出目录（默认 `noir-out`） |
| `--min <score>` | 只保留分数 ≥ N 的应用 |
| `--limit <n>` | 最多输出 N 条 |
| `--only <regex>` | 只扫描匹配的包名，例如 `--only 'com\.miui\.'` |
| `--adb <path>` / `--jadx <path>` | 手动指定工具路径 |
| `--yes` | 自动化场景下跳过确认 |

## DeepScan：一条命令反编译 + 处置

```bash
noir deepscan                  # 反编译风险最高的 15 个应用
noir deepscan --top 30         # 更多
noir deepscan --all            # 全部被标记应用（慢，占磁盘）
noir deepscan --jobs 4         # 并行 jadx 数量
```

流程是：扫描 → 按风险排序 → 逐个 `adb pull` + `jadx` → 统计代码级信号
（`Runtime.exec`、`DexClassLoader`、`setApplicationEnabledSetting`、
`enabled_accessibility_services`、`MediaProjection`、`SystemProperties.set`、
短信/设备标识、WebView 桥、无障碍/通知监听/设备管理员 …）→ 解析清单
（导出组件、明文流量、备份、debuggable）→ 识别 SDK（Umeng/Firebase/AppsFlyer…）
→ 输出 `deepscan.md` / `deepscan.tsv` → 询问是否清理。

```bash
noir deepscan --apply          # 分析后执行安全 appops
noir deepscan --apply --purge  # 再逐个确认卸载高风险用户应用
```

反编译结果按 `包名 + APK 路径` 缓存，第二次跑同一个应用会直接复用。

## 输出

```
noir-out/
├── report.json               # 结构化结果（应用、权限、端点、建议）
├── report.md                 # 人类可读报告
├── domains-trackers.txt      # 统计/广告/崩溃上报，可整份导入
├── domains-other.txt         # 用途不明，导入前逐条判断
├── domains-functional.txt    # 推送/登录/更新/支付/商店/云同步，禁止拦截
├── domains.txt               # 等于 trackers（兼容旧脚本）
├── plan.txt                  # 本次可执行的 appops
└── rollback.txt              # 回滚命令
```

## 隐私

- 工具本身**不联网**：没有遥测、没有版本检查、没有崩溃上报
- 扫描结果只写在你指定的 `--out` 目录
- 唯一的外部请求发生在 `noir setup`（下载 adb/jadx）和 `noir deep`（jadx 是本地进程）
- 报告里可能包含你设备上的包名和端点，分享前自行检查

## 缓存

扫描结果按 `包名 + APK 路径` 缓存在 `~/.noir/endpoints.tsv`。应用更新后路径变化会自动重新分析，重复扫描通常只需几秒。

---

## 架构

```
adb ──▶ pm / dumpsys ──▶ Dumpsys parser ──┐
                                          ├─▶ cache (pkg + apk path)
adb ──▶ unzip/strings ──▶ endpoints ──────┘        │
                                                   ▼
                                          Classifier ─▶ score ─▶ Advisor
                                                   │              │
                                                   ▼              ▼
                                              report.json    plan.txt
                                              report.md      rollback.txt
                                                   │
                                                   ▼
                                                 Tui / CLI
```

`deep` 走另一条支线：`adb pull` → `jadx` → 源码 grep。

## 设计取舍

- **端点抽取在设备端完成**：`adb shell` 内跑 `unzip | strings | grep`，避免把几百个 APK 拉回电脑。设备缺少 `unzip`/`strings` 时自动退化为本地解析。
- **共享 UID 特殊处理**：Android 上 `android.uid.system` 下的应用（常见 50+ 个）权限记录在 `dumpsys package` 尾部的 `Shared users` 段。解析器会把这些权限合并回每个包，否则最该被看见的应用反而会消失。
- **建议分级**：只有 appops 级别的动作标记为可自动执行；卸载必须显式开启。
- **无遥测**：程序不包含任何上报逻辑。

## 常见问题

**需要 root 吗？**
不需要。全部通过 `adb` 的 shell 权限完成；卸载只是 `--user 0` 级别，APK 仍在系统分区。

**会改坏手机吗？**
默认完全只读。`--apply` 只改 app-ops，每条都能用 `default` 还原，`rollback.txt` 会写出来。
`noir block` 的卸载也会先打印 `pm install-existing` 的恢复命令。

**为什么有些应用只给"人工复核"？**
系统应用不能真正卸载（`--user 0` 卸载也会被 OTA 或恢复出厂装回来），所以只建议
app-ops 或 DNS 层拦截。

**DNS 拦截为什么只导出不执行？**
跨平台改 DNS 很容易把设备网断掉（我们在开发中踩过），所以只导出清单：

- `domains-trackers.txt` —— 统计/广告/崩溃上报，可以整份导入
- `domains-other.txt` —— 用途不明，导入前逐条判断
- `domains-functional.txt` —— 推送、登录、更新、支付、应用商店、云同步，**拦了会掉功能**
- `domains.txt` —— 现在只包含 trackers，兼容旧脚本

IP、`localhost` 和带 `test`/`staging` 的域名会被自动剔除。

**支持 iOS 吗？**
不支持。`core` 是按 Kotlin Multiplatform 组织的，但审计逻辑依赖 Android 的
`dumpsys` 和 APK 格式。

## 参与

- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) — 构建、测试、规则放在哪
- [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) — 漏洞报告方式（请不要开公开 issue）
- [Issues](https://github.com/Verlintas/NOIR/issues) — bug 请附上 `noir doctor` 输出

## 路线图

- [x] 等宽仪表盘（`noir ui`）
- [x] DeepScan（批量反编译 + 代码级信号）
- [x] 自带运行时的双击即用包（jpackage）
- [ ] 图形界面（Compose Multiplatform）
- [ ] 规则文件可配置（YAML），支持社区规则包
- [ ] 与 `apktool` / `jadx` 的批量流水线
- [ ] 设备端 DNS/VPN 拦截方案导出
- [ ] 扫描结果签名与版本对比

## 免责声明

NOIR 只应用于**你自己的设备**，或你获得明确授权的设备。它给出的是静态证据
（"这个应用具备这个能力，并且代码里有这个端点"），**不能证明**某次具体传输发生过。
请结合网络层证据自行判断。

## 许可

items.readme:
# teardown

A Claude Code skill that turns any machine into a 3D simulator you can take apart.

Ask how something works. Claude builds it as one offline HTML page: the machine runs in the middle, every panel around it reads the real numbers, a button opens the part doing the work, and when nobody touches it the page tours itself.

![Mellis HB-7 robotic bee simulator](docs/bee.gif)

| Telson SC-8 robotic scorpion | Pelagos OC-8 robotic octopus |
|---|---|
| ![Telson SC-8 robotic scorpion](docs/scorpion.gif) | ![Pelagos OC-8 robotic octopus](docs/octopus.gif) |

## Install

```
npx skills add elvarofficial/teardown -g -a claude-code
```

Then, once, in the installed folder:

```
npm install && npx playwright install chromium
```

You need Node.js 20 or newer. For the video you also need `ffmpeg`, and for the sound Python 3.

## Use

Ask Claude Code in plain words:

> Build me a simulator of a 4-stroke motorcycle engine I can take apart.

> How does a mechanical watch keep time? Show me as a simulator.

> Make a teardown of a hydraulic excavator arm and record a 20-second video of it.

Or open one of the 3 examples first:

```
node sims/build.mjs v8-live          # teardown-out/dist/v8-live.html
node sims/build.mjs cessna-live
node sims/build.mjs strandbeest-live
```

## What is inside

| | |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | What Claude reads: how a machine is built, the rules that make it look right, the review loop. |
| `sims/kit/` | Runtime, stage, shader warm-up. |
| `sims/v8-*`, `sims/cessna-*`, `sims/strandbeest-*` | 3 complete machines. `-shared` is the machine, `-live` the page you drive, `-film` the recorded tour. |
| `sims/build.mjs` | Bundles a machine into one HTML file, three.js and fonts inlined. |
| `sims/capture.mjs` | Renders the film frame by frame to a 60 fps mp4, or to review sheets of stills. |
| `sfx/`, `run_sfx.py` | Procedural sound on the film's timeline, mastered to −14 LUFS. |

## Credits

Built on [whaleyxbt/claude-motion](https://github.com/whaleyxbt/claude-motion) (MIT): the runtime, frame capture, sound engine and review rules come from there. Recorded samples are CC0 from Freesound, prepared by [Barty-Bart/motion-graphics](https://github.com/Barty-Bart/motion-graphics); sources in `sfx/samples/SOURCES.md`.

MIT licence.

items.readme: # terminal-mac [![](https://img.shields.io/static/v1?label=Sponsor&message=%E2%9D%A4&logo=GitHub&color=%23fe8e86)](https://github.com/sponsors/govijr) A separate macOS desktop for computer-use agents, viewed and controlled from a terminal. `terminal-mac` is an early release candidate for Apple silicon. Apple Virtualization runs a real macOS guest. A bundled helper **inside that guest** captures its screen and posts input events. A terminal viewer streams that screen using Kitty or iTerm2 graphics. Agent commands use the same helper without moving the physical Mac's pointer or changing its clipboard. The guest is a separate Mac: it has its own apps, files, accounts and permissions. It does not inherit your running host apps or signed-in sessions. The VM still consumes host CPU, memory and storage. ## Requirements - Apple silicon Mac, macOS 14 or later. - No development tools are needed for a prebuilt release. Maintainers need Xcode 16 or later / Swift 6 to build. - Internet on first run to download macOS directly from Apple, or an existing compatible `.ipsw`. - Space for the cached restore image and a growing VM disk (64 GiB logical size by default). - Ghostty, Kitty or iTerm2 for the inline viewer. Other terminals can use the native VM window and agent CLI. tmux passthrough and automatic terminal splits are not implemented. ## Install and run ```sh curl -fsSL https://github.com/govijr/terminal-mac/releases/latest/download/get.sh | bash ``` The installer downloads the latest release and verifies its SHA-256 before installing. You can also extract a release ZIP and run `bash install.sh` from it. The installer places one launcher in `~/.local/bin` and the bundled runtime under `~/.local/lib/terminal-mac`. Add `~/.local/bin` to your PATH to use simply `terminal-mac`. It needs no administrator rights and does not edit your shell configuration. `bash install.sh --prefix /absolute/path` selects another location. Running `terminal-mac` in an interactive terminal starts the guided flow. `terminal-mac up` does the same explicitly. It automatically downloads/caches a compatible Apple restore image, installs a virtual Mac, boots it and checks the guest helper. Later runs reuse the existing VM and reconnect. Unsupported terminals get the native desktop window. **Current status:** early release candidate. Releases are self-signed (no Apple notarization), which the curl installer doesn't need. Live guest acceptance on a clean Mac is still pending. ## Use with agents terminal-mac gives agents computer use in a separate virtual Mac, through MCP tools (`screenshot`, `click`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type`, `key`, `status`) and a skill that teaches the observe → act → verify loop. **Claude Code**, with the MCP server and skill in one plugin: ```text /plugin install terminal-mac --marketplace govijr/terminal-mac ``` Or add them separately: ```sh claude mcp add terminal-mac -- terminal-mac mcp terminal-mac skills install # → ~/.claude/skills/terminal-mac/SKILL.md ``` **Other MCP clients** (Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Windsurf…): paste the output of `terminal-mac mcp --config` into the client's MCP settings. Use `terminal-mac mcp NAME` for a VM other than `default`. **Any agent with a skills folder:** `terminal-mac skills install --dir PATH`, or `npx skills add govijr/terminal-mac --skill terminal-mac`. In an `AGENTS.md`, a line like "Before using the virtual Mac, run `terminal-mac skills get`" gives the agent instructions that match the installed version. The tools only drive the guest helper. They never touch your own desktop. When the guest is at its login screen, they say so, so the agent can ask you to sign in. ## One-time guest setup The first run opens the virtual Mac's window. Complete macOS setup and create its user account. Inside the guest, open Finder → `/Volumes/My Shared Files/tools` → `TerminalMacGuest.app` once. The helper installs itself in the guest's `~/Applications`, launches that installed copy and registers for future guest logins, subject to macOS approval. Use its two buttons to grant **Screen Recording** and **Accessibility** inside the guest. Reopen it if macOS asks. If needed, its **Guest Login Items** button opens the startup setting. The host needs neither privacy permission. Once both guest permissions are ready, the CLI automatically continues to the terminal desktop. This is guided setup, not an unattended guest installation. Apple documents automatic account provisioning for macOS 27 guests; this build targets the APIs available in the installed macOS 26 SDK and does not implement that newer flow. See [Apple's provisioning documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/virtualization/vzmacguestprovisioningoptions). ```sh terminal-mac up work # another virtual Mac terminal-mac up --ipsw /path/mac.ipsw # use a local image terminal-mac up --no-view # wait for agent readiness, then return JSON terminal-mac up --detach # install/boot, return without waiting for guest setup terminal-mac up --plan # show steps without network access or disk changes ``` The first download may take time; packaging cannot eliminate downloading and installing macOS. The image cache is reused, and URLSession resume data is retained after recoverable network failures. A hard process kill may require the current download to restart. An incomplete installation with recorded hardware can be retried by `up` using a compatible restore image; an already installed VM is never reinstalled by `up`. ## Build from source ```sh bash scripts/build.sh ./dist/terminal-mac doctor ``` The build creates `dist/TerminalMac.app`, including `TerminalMacGuest.app`, and the `dist/terminal-mac` launcher. Virtualization needs the host executable's `com.apple.security.virtualization` entitlement; use the packaged launcher instead of the unsigned Swift build product. It is signed with the self-signed "Govijr Code Signing" identity when your keychain has it (`bash scripts/create-signing-identity.sh` makes one), and ad-hoc otherwise. A stable identity keeps the guest helper's permissions across rebuilds; ad-hoc builds need them granted again. [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) covers signing and publishing. ## Create your first Mac ```sh # Show the URL and version without downloading anything: ./dist/terminal-mac image # Explicitly download Apple's latest supported restore image (several GB): ./dist/terminal-mac image --output /tmp/RestoreImage.ipsw # Install macOS. The disk is sparse, and the IPSW is not copied into the VM bundle. ./dist/terminal-mac create default --ipsw /tmp/RestoreImage.ipsw ./dist/terminal-mac start default --window ``` Complete macOS Setup Assistant in the VM window and create a guest account. Inside the guest: 1. Open Finder → `/Volumes/My Shared Files/tools`. 2. Open `TerminalMacGuest.app`. It installs itself to the guest's `~/Applications` and opens the installed copy. 3. Use the helper's buttons to grant **Screen Recording** and **Accessibility** in the guest's System Settings. Reopen the helper if macOS asks. The host does not need either permission. 4. Keep the guest logged in and the helper running. It registers itself for guest login; approve that setting if macOS requests it. On the host: ```sh ./dist/terminal-mac action default status ./dist/terminal-mac hide default ./dist/terminal-mac view default ``` The viewer supports typing, left/right clicks, double and triple clicks, dragging, scrolling, arrows and common control keys. **Ctrl+G** opens a palette of Mac shortcuts (Spotlight, Mission Control, copy/paste, close/quit and more), because terminals keep ⌘ for themselves. **Ctrl+]** exits the viewer while the VM keeps running. Closing the native VM window hides it and also leaves the VM running. The guest helper keeps a ScreenCaptureKit stream open while a viewer is watching. It sends a frame only when the screen changes (up to 30 fps), already sized to the pixels the terminal draws, as lossless lz4-compressed pixels. Kitty and Ghostty receive those frames through shared memory rather than the pty. An idle desktop costs nothing, and the stream stops 15 seconds after the viewer leaves. From build 4 on, the guest helper updates itself: within 30 seconds of a newer build appearing in the shared tools folder, it installs that build and relaunches. Helpers from build 3 and earlier still work but poll full screenshots, and the header shows "snapshots". Update those once by opening `/Volumes/My Shared Files/tools/TerminalMacGuest.app` in the guest. Releases are signed with one unchanging self-signed certificate, so the guest keeps its Screen Recording and Accessibility approvals across updates. Agents can drive the guest through an MCP server: `claude mcp add terminal-mac -- "$PWD/dist/terminal-mac" mcp default`. See [docs/AGENT.md](docs/AGENT.md). New VMs use a 2x HiDPI display (for example 2560×1600 pixels at 220 ppi for the default 1280×800 points), so text stays sharp on Retina terminals. Switch a stopped VM with `terminal-mac display default --hidpi` or `--standard`. The automounted volume is supplied by macOS virtio-fs. If it is absent, check the guest's macOS version and the VM log; this prototype has no fallback guest transport. ## Give an agent computer control ```sh ./dist/terminal-mac action default screenshot --output /tmp/guest.png ./dist/terminal-mac action default click 640 400 ./dist/terminal-mac action default type 'Hello from the agent' ./dist/terminal-mac action default key cmd+space ./dist/terminal-mac action default key return ./dist/terminal-mac action default scroll --dy -300 --x 640 --y 400 ``` Commands return JSON and a nonzero exit status on failure. Screenshots return a local host PNG path. Coordinates start at the top-left and match the screenshot's dimensions; screenshots use guest display points to keep input coordinates consistent on Retina displays. `snapshot` is currently a screenshot alias, not an accessibility-tree snapshot. The agent instructions are in [docs/AGENT.md](docs/AGENT.md). No global agent settings are modified. ## Lifecycle and resources ```sh ./dist/terminal-mac ls ./dist/terminal-mac status default ./dist/terminal-mac pause default ./dist/terminal-mac resume default ./dist/terminal-mac show default ./dist/terminal-mac stop default # request a normal guest shutdown ./dist/terminal-mac stop default --force # immediate power-off; unsaved guest work can be lost ``` Customize a new VM with `--cpus 4 --memory 4 --disk 64 --width 1280 --height 800` (width and height are in points; add `--standard` for a 1x display). CPU, memory and disk arguments are logical CPUs, GiB and GiB respectively. `--offline` omits the guest network device; the shared-folder control channel still works, though some macOS setup workflows may require networking. VM data lives in `~/Library/Application Support/terminal-mac/machines/NAME/`. `TERMINAL_MAC_HOME` overrides the data root. Each VM has an exclusive file lock, a sparse disk, hardware identity, auxiliary boot storage, `machine.json`, a private host-control mailbox, the guest exchange directory, and `runtime.log`. A VM boot runs as a separate background process. Lifecycle commands must use the same `TERMINAL_MAC_HOME` as the process that started it. An interrupted or failed installation leaves its directory and `installed: false` for diagnosis. It is never silently overwritten. To retry, ensure no installer/VM is running, move that incomplete directory aside, then create the VM again. There is deliberately no destructive VM-delete command yet. ## Isolation model - Host input and screen APIs are not used for agent actions. The helper refuses to run unless `hw.model` starts with `VirtualMac`. That check prevents accidental host execution; it is not hardware attestation or a defense against a compromised host. - The guest sees two explicit shares: `control` (read/write, containing request/reply JSON and screenshots) and `tools` (read-only helper app). Host home, project folders, clipboard, microphone, and camera are not attached. - There is no remote-control network listener. The flat mailbox pins its directory, rejects symlinks, hardlinks and nonregular files on reads, bounds message sizes, checks request IDs, and expires pending actions. The host never executes guest-provided content. - Default NAT networking permits guest internet access and may reach services on the host or local network. This is **not** a network-isolated or hardened hostile-code environment. `--offline` removes that network path. - A logged-out/locked guest, missing helper, denied guest permissions, or paused VM prevents normal computer use. TCC grants are interactive guest setup, not bypassed by the CLI. VM cloning, rollback checkpoints, accessibility snapshots, fully unattended guest setup, terminal splits and tmux transport remain future work. The native Virtualization framework does not itself render a Mac into a terminal or offer an agent input API; this project supplies the guest transport and terminal presentation layers. ## Development and validation ```sh CLANG_MODULE_CACHE_PATH=/tmp/terminal-mac-modules \ SWIFTPM_MODULECACHE_OVERRIDE=/tmp/terminal-mac-modules \ swift test --disable-sandbox --scratch-path /tmp/terminal-mac-build \ --cache-path /tmp/terminal-mac-cache \ --config-path /tmp/terminal-mac-config --security-path /tmp/terminal-mac-security ``` Tests cover mailbox round trips, expiry and cleanup, file-boundary defenses, name/option validation, fragmented UTF-8 and terminal input sequences. These are automated protocol checks, not evidence that a guest was installed, booted, granted permissions, or controlled successfully. See [docs/VALIDATION.md](docs/VALIDATION.md) for recorded results and the live checklist. References: [terminal-browser](https://terminal-browser.com/), [Apple's macOS virtualization sample](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/virtualization/running-macos-in-a-virtual-machine-on-apple-silicon), [VZVirtualMachineView](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/virtualization/vzvirtualmachineview), [ScreenCaptureKit](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/screencapturekit). ## Sponsor terminal-mac is free and maintained in my own time. [Sponsoring](https://github.com/sponsors/govijr) keeps it that way.

Dev tooling, not just clouds

AI apps

items.readme:
# Claude Animated Shorts

The free Claude skill from the video **"How to Make Viral Animated Shorts Using Claude (Full Workflow)"**.

It makes 55-70 s vertical animated story shorts: 2D characters in a colourful 3D world, with ink outlines, a painted town, lens blur, gliding cameras, a march score and sound effects. Everything is rendered with three.js inside Remotion on your own PC, with no AI video generator.

Proven on **The Bridge That Fell for a Song**, a 67 s short about the 1831 Broughton bridge.

## What's inside
| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `SKILL.md` | The skill: the full pipeline, every rule, every fix, and the final look values |
| `templates/bridge/` | The full source of the bridge short: world, characters, ink, lens blur, grade, story/camera |
| `templates/audio/` | The synthesized sound: SFX, march music, the mix with ducking and loudness |
| `templates/scripts/` | Stills, side-by-side sheets, shot merge and frame-by-frame QA helpers |
| `references/STYLE_BIBLE.md` | The script and visual formula measured from 20 reference shorts |
| `references/reports/` | Seven measured reports: motion, depth, textures, characters, lighting, outlines, grade |
| `references/frames/` | 38 full-size reference frames (540x960) to compare your frames against |
| `references/sheets/` | 20 contact sheets, one per reference short, 60 frames each (1,200 frames) |

## Install
1. Copy this folder to `~/.claude/skills/cartoon-3d-short/` (clone it there, or download the ZIP).
2. You need [Remotion](https://www.remotion.dev/) with `@remotion/three`, plus Node, Python 3 and ffmpeg.
3. In Claude Code, say: *"Use the cartoon short skill and make a short about …"*.

Claude then follows `SKILL.md`: topic and facts, then script, then voice, then the shot plan in `story.ts`, then stills, then renders. Agents check your frames against the reports and the frames, and you get the final 2K render and sound mix.

## Notes
- Set `REMOTION_TMP` to a folder on a big drive. Every Remotion bundle copies `public/` (~1.3 GB) into the temp folder.
- Story, characters and voice should always be your own. Use the references for the look, not the content.

## License
The code and docs are MIT (see `LICENSE`). The reference frames are included for style study only.

items.name: hop
items.description: Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick
items.readme:
Install Linux next to Windows without a USB stick.

## What it is hop is a single Windows app that installs Linux alongside Windows. Pick a system, choose a drive, drag to choose how much space it gets, and click Install. There's no USB stick to find and nothing to install first. ## What it does - **Downloads from official sources.** It gets the ISO from the project's own server and verifies its checksum where the project publishes one. You can also use an ISO you already have. - **Makes room safely.** It checks your PC first, and nothing on the disk changes until those checks pass. - **Frees space that's stuck.** A drive can show plenty free and still refuse to shrink, because of files Windows can't move. Make room clears them in one click and puts your settings back afterwards. - **Goes where there's room.** Shrink C: or another drive, use free space, or use a second disk inside the PC. If C: is full, hop suggests a drive that isn't, and the download can go elsewhere too. - **Tells you what to click.** It lists the exact choices to make in the Linux installer. - **Gets you unstuck.** If the PC goes back to Windows, reopening hop explains why and can restart into the BIOS. - **Cleans up after itself.** Undo gives the space back to the drive it came from, and it can also remove another Linux already on the drive. - **Can replace Windows entirely, for the systems where hop has seen it work:** Ubuntu, Xubuntu, Ubuntu Budgie, Ubuntu Cinnamon, Edubuntu, Ubuntu Studio, Zorin OS, Fedora Workstation, Ultramarine, elementary OS, Debian, Arch and Omarchy. It's a separate choice with its own warning, and you have to type ERASE. hop only makes the installer, which copies itself to memory so it can erase the disk it started from when you tell it to. It needs more memory than the ISO's size, and it's only offered for systems where hop has seen it erase a disk and start again afterwards. **Systems:** elementary OS, Ubuntu and its flavours (Budgie, Xubuntu, Lubuntu, Cinnamon, Unity, Edubuntu, Studio), Linux Mint, Pop!_OS, Zorin OS, Debian, Fedora Workstation, Ultramarine, CachyOS, Arch Linux and Omarchy. Other Ubuntu-based ISOs should work too, if you choose the file yourself. Kubuntu isn't supported, because its ISO has a file too big for FAT32. CachyOS, Arch, Omarchy and Pop!_OS need Secure Boot off. Omarchy also needs BitLocker fully off on its disk, not paused, and hop refuses until it is. hop won't turn it off for you. Debian, CachyOS, Linux Mint and Zorin OS can't go on a second disk yet. **Needs:** Windows 10 (1803 or newer) or 11, on a UEFI PC with a GPT disk, which is nearly every PC sold with them. Linux has to go on a disk inside the PC, not a USB drive.

## How it works A USB installer is just a FAT32 drive with the ISO's files on it. hop makes the same thing on your internal disk: ``` Before [ EFI ][ C: Windows ][ Recovery ] After [ EFI ][ C: Windows ][ Installer ][ Linux ][ Recovery ] ``` 1. **Download and check** the ISO, and confirm it's a system hop can install. 2. **Make room** after the drive you chose, using free space first and shrinking the drive only if needed. 3. **Copy** the ISO's files onto a small FAT32 partition, and check each one. 4. **Add a startup entry** with the ISO's signed boot loader, for the next restart only. 5. **Restart.** The Linux installer opens and installs into the space hop made. More detail is in [How hop works](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). ## Use it Download `hop.exe` from [Releases](../../releases) and run it. Windows asks for administrator access, and SmartScreen may warn because hop isn't code-signed yet: click **More info → Run anyway**. If something goes wrong, see [Troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md). ## Build it You need the .NET SDK, on any OS. The result is `bin/Release/hop.exe`. ``` dotnet build -c Release ``` See [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) to help, or to add a Linux system. ## License [MIT](LICENSE). Instrument Sans is under the SIL Open Font License. Linux logos belong to their projects and are listed in [SOURCES.md](assets/logos/SOURCES.md). hop isn't affiliated with any of them.
